title.en: Salutation to Sandhyā and the deities (Samaṣṭi-abhivādanam)

intro: Stand with hands in añjali mudrā and turn clockwise, saluting the four directions in turn. Morning and noon: begin facing east (east → south → west → north). Evening: begin facing west (west → north → east → south). Return to the starting direction for the last two mantras.

items.action: face east (evening: west), hands in añjali
items.meaning: Salutations to Sandhyā, the goddess of the junctures of the day.
Salutations again and again to all the deities.
I did not of my own accord commit sin; falling under the sway of desire and anger I sinned unwittingly. Forgive me — I pay my obeisance again and again.

intro: Bend forward at the waist, cross the forearms (right over left) and touch the ears with the hands; state your lineage and name. Then touch the ground (or the feet of elders present) and stand erect. Fill in your own pravara ṛṣis, gotra, sūtra and name; the app substitutes them from your settings.

text.iast: abhivādaye {pravara} {arsheya} pravarānvita {gotra} gotraḥ {sutra} sūtraḥ yajuśśākhādhyāyī śrī {name} śarmā nāmāham asmi bhoḥ ||

items.action: bend forward, hands crossed touching the ears; then touch the ground
items.meaning: I salute — I, of the pravara of the ṛṣis {pravara}, of the {gotra} gotra, of the {sutra} sūtra, a student of the Yajur śākhā, named {name} śarmā.

items.text: After the pravara ṛṣis say *trayārṣeya* if your pravara has three ṛṣis and *pañcārṣeya* if it has five (see the gotra–pravara table). Worked example (Sandhyavandanam.pdf): *abhivādaye vaiśvāmitra āghamarṣaṇa kauśika trayārṣeya pravarānvita kauśika gotraḥ āpastamba sūtraḥ yajuś śākhādhyāyī śrī lakṣmīnārāyaṇa śarmā nāmāham asmi bhoḥ*.

intro: Turn clockwise again as before, hands in añjali. Morning and noon start from the east and end with the north; evening starts from the west and ends with the south. Then, facing the starting direction, point the joined palms up and down alternately for the remaining salutations.

items.action: face east (evening: west); joined palms pointing up, look above
joined palms pointing down, look below
palms up, look towards the sky
palms down, look towards the earth
palms down / straight ahead; think of the Lord in the orb of the Sun

intro: Face south, hands in añjali, and contemplating Yama, the Lord of Death, recite.

text.iast:
yamāya dharmarājāya mṛtyave cāntakāya ca |
vaivasvatāya kālāya sarvabhūtakṣayāya ca ||
audumbarāya dadhnāya nīlāya parameṣṭhine |
vṛkodarāya citrāya citraguptāya vai namaḥ ||
citraguptāya vai nama oṃ nama iti ||

items.meaning: Salutations to Yama, King Dharma, Death, the Ender, the son of Vivasvān (the Sun), Time, the destroyer of all beings; to Audumbara, Dadhna, the blue-hued one, the supreme lord, the insatiable one, the wondrous one, and to Citragupta who records all deeds — salutations.

title.en: Prayer to Śiva as the universal form (Harihara vandanam)

intro: Face north, hands in añjali, and recite.

text.iast:
ṛ̱taguṃ sa̱tyaṃ pa̍raṃ bra̱hma̱ pu̱ruṣa̍ṃ kṛṣṇa̱ piṅga̍lam |
ū̱rdhvare̍taṃ vi̍rūpā̱kṣa̱ṃ vi̱śvarū̍pāya̱ vai namo̱ nama̍ḥ ||
viśvarūpāya vai nama oṃ nama iti ||

items.meaning: The Cosmic Order, the Truth, the Supreme Brahman — the Person dark-blue and tawny, of restrained seed, three-eyed: salutations again and again to Him of universal form.

title.en: Salutation to Narmadā and protection from serpents

intro: Some families add this, facing east. Recite with hands in añjali.

text.iast:
narmadāyai namaḥ prātar narmadāyai namo niśi |
namo 'stu narmade tubhyaṃ trāhi māṃ viṣasarpataḥ ||
apasarpa sarpa bhadraṃ te dūraṃ gaccha mahāyaśaḥ |
janamejayasya yajñānte āstīka vacanaṃ smaran ||
jaratkārvor jaratkārvāṃ samutpanno mahāyaśaḥ |
āstīkassatyasandho māṃ pannagebhyo 'bhirakṣatu ||
pannagebhyo 'bhirakṣatu oṃ nama iti ||

items.meaning: Salutation to Narmadā by day, salutation to Narmadā by night; salutations to you, Narmadā — protect me from venomous serpents. Go away, serpent — blessings on you — go far, O renowned one, remembering Āstīka's word at the end of Janamejaya's sacrifice. May Āstīka of great renown, true to his vow, born of Jaratkāru and Jaratkāru, protect me from serpents.

title.en: Salutation to Nārāyaṇa in the Sun

intro: Face the Sun (east in the morning and at noon, west in the evening) with hands in añjali and, meditating on Nārāyaṇa in the solar orb, recite.

text.iast:
namaḥ savitre jagadeka cakṣuṣe jagat prasūti sthiti nāśa hetave |
trayīmayāya triguṇātma dhāriṇe viriñci nārāyaṇa śaṅkarātmane ||

items.meaning: Salutations to Savitṛ, the sole eye of the world, the cause of the creation, sustenance and dissolution of the universe, who is the three Vedas, who bears the three guṇas, and who is of the nature of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and Śaṅkara.

text.iast:
dhyeyassadā savitṛ maṇḍala madhyavartī nārāyaṇaḥ sarasijāsana sanniviṣṭaḥ |
keyūravān makara kuṇḍalavān kirīṭī hārī hiraṇmaya vapuḥ dhṛta śaṅkha cakraḥ ||

items.meaning: Nārāyaṇa, seated in the centre of the solar orb on a lotus seat, is ever to be meditated upon — adorned with armlets, makara earrings, crown and necklace, of golden body, holding the conch and discus.

text.iast:
śaṅkha cakra gadā pāṇe dvārakā nilayācyuta |
govinda puṇḍarīkākṣa rakṣa māṃ śaraṇāgatam ||

items.meaning: O wielder of conch, discus and mace, dweller in Dvārakā, Acyuta, Govinda, lotus-eyed one — protect me who have taken refuge in You.

text.iast:
ākāśāt patitaṃ toyaṃ yathā gacchati sāgaram |
sarvadeva namaskāraḥ keśavaṃ prati gacchati ||
keśavaṃ prati gacchaty oṃ nama iti ||

items.meaning: Just as water fallen from the sky reaches the ocean, so salutation to any god reaches Keśava alone.

text.iast:
namo brahmaṇya devāya go brāhmaṇa hitāya ca |
jagaddhitāya kṛṣṇāya govindāya namo namaḥ ||

items.meaning: Salutations again and again to the God of the brāhmaṇas, the well-wisher of cows and brāhmaṇas, the well-wisher of the world — to Kṛṣṇa, to Govinda.

items.text: Chakravarthy marks *namo brahmaṇya devāya* optional and prescribes four sāṣṭāṅga namaskārams (full prostrations) after this vandanam.

intro: Repeat the abhivādanam exactly as before — bend forward, hands crossed touching the ears, state your lineage and name, touch the ground. Then sit and perform ācamanam (*acyutāya namaḥ, anantāya namaḥ, govindāya namaḥ* and the twelve names).

text.iast: abhivādaye {pravara} {arsheya} pravarānvita {gotra} gotraḥ {sutra} sūtraḥ yajuśśākhādhyāyī śrī {name} śarmā nāmāham asmi bhoḥ ||

items.action: bend forward, hands crossed touching the ears; then touch the ground
items.meaning: I salute — I, of the pravara of the ṛṣis {pravara}, of the {gotra} gotra, of the {sutra} sūtra, a student of the Yajur śākhā, named {name} śarmā.

intro: Sit down. Take a little water in the right palm and, reciting, let it fall to the ground, dedicating everything done to Nārāyaṇa. Śrī Vaiṣṇavas first close the rite with the sātvika tyāgam (hands in añjali).

text.iast: bhagavāneva svaniyāmya svarūpasthiti pravṛtti svaśeṣataika rasena anena ātmanā kartrā svakīyaiśca upakaraṇaiḥ svārādhanaika prayojanāya paramapuruṣaḥ sarvaśeṣī śriyaḥ patiḥ svaśeṣabhūtaṃ idaṃ {kala} sandhyāvandanākhyaṃ karma svasmai svaprītaye svayameva kāritavān ||

items.meaning: The Lord Himself — the Supreme Person, master of all, consort of Śrī — through this self of mine as the doer, whose form, existence and activity He governs and whose sole essence is to be His subordinate, and with His own instruments, for the sole purpose of His own worship, has caused this {kalaEn} sandhyāvandanam, which belongs to Him, to be performed for Himself, for His own pleasure.

text.iast:
śrīraṅga maṅgalamaṇiṃ karuṇā nivāsam śrī veṅkaṭādri śikharālaya kālamegham |
śrī hastiśaila śikharojvala pārijātam śrīśaṃ namāmi śirasā yaduśailadīpam ||

items.meaning: I bow my head to the Lord of Śrī — the auspicious jewel of Śrīraṅgam, abode of compassion; the dark rain-cloud dwelling on the peak of Veṅkaṭādri; the pārijāta shining on the summit of Hastiśaila (Kāñcī); the lamp of Yadu hill (Melkoṭe).

items.text: Chakravarthy gives this verse as optional (for Ahobila Maṭha śiṣyas); Kidambi includes it for all.

text.iast:
kāyena vācā manasendriyair vā buddhyātmanā vā prakṛteḥ svabhāvāt |
karomi yad yat sakalaṃ parasmai nārāyaṇāyeti samarpayāmi ||

items.action: water in the right palm; let it fall to the ground
items.meaning: Whatever I do with body, speech, mind or senses, with the intellect or the self, or by the very nature of my disposition — all that I offer to the Supreme Nārāyaṇa.

text.iast:
mantrahīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ bhaktihīnaṃ janārdana |
yat kṛtaṃ tu mayā deva paripūrṇaṃ tad astu te ||

items.meaning: Deficient as it is in mantra, in method and in devotion, O Janārdana — whatever has been done by me, O God, may it be complete for You.

text.iast:
prāyaścittāny aśeṣāṇi tapaḥ karmātmakāni vai |
yāni teṣām aśeṣāṇāṃ kṛṣṇānusmaraṇaṃ param ||
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa |

items.meaning: Of all the expiations consisting of austerity and ritual action, the highest of them all is the remembrance of Kṛṣṇa.

title.en: Conclusion: sprinkling the place of japa

intro: Take a little water in the hand and sprinkle it on the spot where you sat for the sandhyāvandanam. Touch the sprinkled water with the right ring finger and apply it to the forehead as tilakam. Conclude with brahmārpaṇam, ācamanam and prostration.

text.iast:
a̱dyā no̍ deva savitaḥ pra̱jāva̍t sāvī̱ḥ saubha̍gam | parā̍ du̱ḥṣvapniyagu̍ṃ suva ||
oṃ viśvā̎ni deva savitar duri̱tāni parā̍ suva | yad bha̱draṃ tanna̱ āsu̍va ||

items.action: sprinkle water on the place of japa; touch it and apply to the forehead
items.meaning: Send us this day, O God Savitṛ, prosperity with progeny; drive away from us the evil dream. O God Savitṛ, drive away from us all sins and misfortunes; send us what is good.

items.action: sprinkle water on the place of the sandhyāvandanam (Kidambi's form)

items.text: Kidambi performs this sprinkling and the ten *śrī kṛṣṇāya namaḥ* immediately after the second abhivādanam and ācamanam, before the sātvika tyāgam and *kāyena vācā*.

items.meaning: Om, That is Truth — may this be an offering to Brahman.

items.text: Perform ācamanam (with the twelve names). Finally prostrate — sāṣṭāṅga namaskāram; Chakravarthy prescribes four prostrations. This completes the {kalaEn} sandhyāvandanam.
